data.description: samples built from real Loghub log lines, arranged into incidents

severity.note: Fresh windows of the training systems. Rules and features were developed on its validation seeds, including rules version 2026.11.3 and lexicon 2.2 (docs/validation-log.md records every candidate run); the published test seeds were never used to choose anything. A regression tripwire, not a measure of new systems.

generalisation.note: Each system and failure mode held out in turn. The per-level calibration, the novelty check, lexicon version 2 and the rule changes of 2026-11-01, and the patterns-beside-lines, cancellation, baseline and unlevelled-line changes of rules version 2026.11.3, were chosen on held-out-system folds of validation seeds 51-56; the published folds use the test seeds, never used to choose anything.

real.hdfs.note: Looked at during development before this record began (2026-10-31). HDFS lines are also in the training pools; the report gives the overlap.

real.bgl.note: Looked at during development before this record began. BGL lines and the same alert-tag rubric are in training, so the report also rates it with a model fitted without BGL.

real.hadoop.note: Every healthy job was flagged once the training-range guard sent these fast-logging jobs to the rules. That led to the crash rule reading warnings and errors only; the change was checked on validation seeds and held-out systems, not on these jobs.

real.openstack.note: A regression found here on 2026-10-31 (healthy runs rated SEV1) led to the training-range guard, whose setting was chosen on validation seeds only.

real.logchunks.note: Looked at during development before this record began.

real.uci_tickets.note: Looked at during development before this record began.

real.gitlab.note: Looked at during development before this record began.

real.postmortems.note: Looked at during development before this record began.

injection_benchmarks.note: Looked at during development before this record began.

redteam.note: Adaptive injection attacks seeded from the public benchmarks (or the edge-case suite's own), mutated until they get past the guard and scored on what they achieve, with the guard and with it bypassed. Its first run showed look-alike letters carrying orders past the guard, and the guard was taught to fold them (2026-11-01), so the guard's own counts here are no longer a blind test; the outcomes after the guard, which are what it gates, were never tuned on.

domains.ait-ads.note: Security alerts from attacked networks (AIT-ADS). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.

domains.rcaeval.note: Code-level faults in microservice shops (RCAEval RE3). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.

domains.anomod.note: Anomalies in two microservice systems at four levels (AnoMod). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.

domains.itbench.note: Kubernetes incidents (ITBench-Lite). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.

domains.nezha.note: Faults injected into Online Boutique's pods (Nezha). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.

domains.jira.note: Human-set priority on public Jira issues (Public Jira Dataset subset). Scored once while the suite was built, before the rule changes of 2026-11-01; nothing was chosen by looking at it.
